title: Add Box Plot Chart Mark

complexity.rationale: The five-number-summary statistics (min/q1/median/q3/max) are computable via Vega's built-in aggregate transform quantile ops, and outlier detection is the well-known Tukey 1.5×IQR method — no deep algorithmic unknowns. But 'auto-detect raw observations vs. precomputed summary' is a genuine, non-precedented design decision (inspecting the incoming data shape to choose a code path) with no existing analog elsewhere in this codebase, and outliers must be rendered as a separate, non-interactive data source layered against the same category scale.

summary: A category-to-distribution mark rendering a box (q1–q3), whiskers (min/max within 1.5×IQR), a median line, and separately-rendered non-interactive outlier points. Accepts either raw per-category observations (aggregated internally) or a precomputed five-number summary per category.
requirements: Accepts a `category` channel plus either: (a) a raw `value` field with many rows per category, aggregated internally into min/q1/median/q3/max, or (b) precomputed `min`/`q1`/`median`/`q3`/`max` fields, one row per category
Auto-detects which mode the incoming data is in without requiring an explicit prop — based on whether the precomputed summary fields are present on the data
Renders a box for the q1–q3 interquartile range, a median line, and whiskers extending to the most extreme in-range values (Tukey 1.5×IQR rule)
Outliers (values beyond 1.5×IQR from the box) render as separate points, non-interactive (no hover/tooltip on individual outlier points)
One box per category value along the dimension axis

edgeCases.case: A category with a single raw observation
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: q1/median/q3 collapse to that single value; box renders as a degenerate zero-height rect rather than throwing on a divide-by-zero IQR.

edgeCases.case: IQR of zero (all values in a category identical)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: No outliers should be flagged even though 1.5×0 = 0, since every value equals the median — avoid a false-positive outlier flood from floating point noise.

edgeCases.case: Data ambiguously matches both raw and precomputed shapes
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Precomputed fields take precedence if present, documented explicitly as the tie-break rule for the auto-detection logic.
Category (x) scale band-width shrinks per existing categorical-scale behavior; no new overflow handling needed.
Box fill/outlier point color resolve through the existing colorScheme-aware static color value.
S1-only for this spec; no S2 port until the mark stabilizes out of rc status.
Hover/tooltip targets the box (summary) mark only; outlier points must not intercept hover events meant for the box beneath them.

crossCutting.notes: touchesHoverAnimation: box/whisker marks reuse the standard isAnimate-gated enter transition already used by rect/rule marks elsewhere. touchesTooltipOrPopover: the box mark should support ChartTooltip/ChartPopover showing the five-number summary, reusing the existing interactive-mark plumbing; outlier points are explicitly excluded from this (isInteractive: false on that layer). requiresNewSignalOrScale: false — uses a standard categorical x scale and linear y scale, same helpers as Bar. requiresS1S2Parity: false because this ships as a new s1-only rc-status mark, matching the Donut/BigNumber precedent; revisit once promoted out of rc.

implementationPlan.change: Create BoxPlotOptions/BoxPlotOptionsWithDefaults/BoxPlotSpecOptions supporting both raw (`category`, `value`) and precomputed (`category`, `min`, `q1`, `median`, `q3`, `max`) field sets as optional/mutually-informing options.
Export the new Box Plot types.
Add BoxPlotOptions to the MarkOptions union.
Two fixtures: defaultBoxPlotOptions (raw-observation mode) and a precomputed-summary variant, for use across both data-shape test paths.

New: detectSummaryMode (inspects options for precomputed field names vs raw value field), addSummaryAggregate (Vega aggregate transform with q1/median/q3/min/max ops for raw mode), addIqrOutlierFlags (formula transform computing 1.5×IQR bounds, then a filter/derived field splitting in-range vs outlier rows) — no existing util to reuse, this is new logic.
getBoxMark (rect for q1–q3), getWhiskerMarks (rule marks to min/max-within-range), getMedianMark (tick/rule), getOutlierMarks (non-interactive symbol layer).

addBoxPlot, addData (branches on detectSummaryMode), addSignals (interactive-mark signals for the box layer only), setScales (categorical dimension scale + linear value scale, reusing addMetricScale).
Unit tests for detectSummaryMode, addSummaryAggregate, addIqrOutlierFlags covering both data shapes.
Unit tests for each mark-factory function using both fixtures.
Register boxPlotCount: -1 in initializeComponentCounts, import addBoxPlot, add the 'boxPlot' switch case.
BoxPlotProps/BoxPlotElement, Omit-ing only fields replaced at the React boundary (ChartTooltip/ChartPopover children).
Render-null component holding prop defaults, placed under rc/ per the Donut/BigNumber rc-status precedent.
Import BoxPlot from '../rc' and add its displayName dispatch case.
Add BoxPlot to the sanitizeRscChartChildren import/list from '../rc'.
Update the toStrictEqual ChartOptions snapshot to include the new mark type at default values.
Two stories: RawObservations and PrecomputedSummary, exercising both auto-detected data shapes.

openQuestions: Exact field-presence rule for auto-detecting precomputed-summary mode — e.g. is it 'all five of min/q1/median/q3/max are present as top-level keys on every row', or a separate explicit marker field?
Should outlier points support their own tooltip in a future iteration, or is non-interactivity a permanent constraint of this mark?
